plan.topic: Constipated on tirzepatide? Why piling on fibre all at once can backfire, and the 'slow fibre plus fluids' approach
plan.angle: Title: 'Tirzepatide Constipation: Why Fibre Too Fast Can Backfire'. Opening: 'Backed up on tirzepatide, so you load up on fibre all at once? Adding a lot quickly can make bloating and discomfort worse. General constipation advice, like the NHS's, is to build fibre up gradually and drink fluids with it.' Then give one SURMOUNT-1 arm vs placebo, copied from L1's verified script. Add the advisory's 'first few days' high-fibre note, framed as being about nausea. Fluids: 'unless your doctor has told you to limit fluids'. Ask your pharmacist or prescriber before using any laxative, with no product names. Red flag, in label wording: severe stomach pain that won't go away means contact your healthcare provider. Then the don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line. Last line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide Constipation: Why More Fibre Can Backfire #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1: the funnel Short that sends people to today's Lane A long-form. It's a myth-bust hook with a tirzepatide-first title. | fact-check: This is a good funnel spin-off with a distinct question. The claim is well supported as general advice: NHS and NIDDK constipation guidance says to increase fibre gradually and drink fluids, because a sudden increase can cause gas and bloating. But it isn't tirzepatide-specific evidence, so attribute it to general constipation advice, not to 'experts' and not to tirzepatide trials. The working title 'Why More Fibre Can Backfire' could be heard as 'fibre is bad', when the video's message is 'too much, too fast'. Tighten it so the payoff matches. The SURMOUNT-1 number must match L1's verified figures exactly (arm, n, placebo, no diabetes, 72 weeks). Keep the advisory's high-fibre note at its exact scope: the first few days of treatment, to ease nausea.

package.description:
Piling on fibre too fast can mean more gas symptoms, like bloating. General advice: build fibre up gradually, with fluids, unless your doctor has told you to limit fluids. In SURMOUNT-1 (adults without diabetes, with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, 72 weeks), constipation was reported in 17.1% of 636 on tirzepatide 10 mg vs 5.8% of 643 on placebo.
Sources: SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35658024/ · NHS Constipation https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/constipation/
#tirzepatide #GLP1 #constipation
Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Backed up on tirzepatide? Piling on fibre fast can backfire with more gas and bloating.

In SURMOUNT-1 (adults without diabetes, with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, over 72 weeks), constipation was reported in 17.1% of 636 people on tirzepatide 10 mg, versus 5.8% of 643 on placebo.

• Ask your pharmacist or prescriber before any laxative

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against its source and they all hold up. SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM 2022, PubMed 35658024) enrolled adults without diabetes who had a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition. It tested tirzepatide 5, 10 or 15 mg against placebo for 72 weeks. Constipation was 17.1% on the 10 mg dose (n=636) versus 5.8% on placebo (n=643), which matches the published adverse-event data. The NHS page (reviewed 26 Oct 2023) says to "gradually increase the fibre in your diet" and "drink plenty of water and other fluids". It also suggests speaking to a pharmacist about laxatives. NIDDK's constipation page (May 2018) says to add fibre "a little at a time". NIDDK's gas page (June 2021) says "some people have more gas symptoms when they consume too much fiber." The AJCN 2025 joint advisory citation is correct, and its first-few-days nausea tip is kept to the wording in the house notes. The fluid-restriction caveat, the ask-before-a-laxative line and the label-style red-flag line are all present, as are the don't-stop line, "Not personal advice", the prescriber line and the approved CTA. The title is paid off: the script lands on "too much, too fast", not "fibre is bad". There are two minor wording fixes and one optional context fix below. None of them would mislead a viewer.

issues.claim: Too much fibre can bring more gas and bloating.
issues.problem: Neither cited page uses the word 'bloating'. NIDDK's gas page says 'more gas symptoms', and the constipation page says nothing about gas or bloating. Bloating counts as a gas symptom on NIDDK's site, so this is only a small wording drift.
issues.fix: Narration: "Understandable. But too much fibre can mean more gas symptoms, like bloating." On-screen: "Too much fibre: more gas symptoms"

issues.claim: Severe stomach pain that won't go away? Contact your healthcare provider right away.
issues.problem: The label lists this symptom (with or without vomiting) as a possible pancreatitis sign. Its full instruction also tells people to stop the medicine and call right away. Our script leaves out the stop instruction, which follows channel rules, and then says 'don't stop on your own'. Adding the vomiting qualifier keeps the line closer to the label without giving stopping advice.
issues.fix: s8 narration: "Severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting? Contact your healthcare provider right away." Keep the on-screen text as it is.

issues.claim: On the ten milligram dose, constipation: 17.1% of 636 vs 5.8% of 643.
issues.problem: The numbers are correct and the arm is labelled. But 10 mg had the highest constipation rate of the three doses (5 mg 16.8%, 15 mg 11.7%). Optional context for viewers on other doses.
issues.fix: Optional: add to the s4 items list: "Other doses: 16.8% (5 mg), 11.7% (15 mg)". The narration can stay as it is.

audio.soundNotes: Music under voice was already close to target (-13.5 dB); nudged it up slightly (+1 dB) mainly to lift the pause level (-16.3 → ~-15) toward the -14 dB felt-swell target without pushing speech-under level past -12. Trimmed redundant simultaneous SFX pairs (pop+tick, pop+whip, swoosh+whoosh duplicates) at six crowded moments (t≈13, 36, 44, 49, 53, 60, 63, 72, 72.2) to stay within the 3–4-effects-per-second rule, and pulled down three cues that were sitting too loud over speech (i11 swoosh, i16 swoosh, i25 tick, the last from -8.9 dB down to a felt level). Boosted the pause-positioned swell (i18) to max and the following ding (i20) ahead of the "17.1% vs 5.8%" stat so the key reveal gets a clear accent, and added five bespoke textures (opening rustle, a gentle digestive gurgle for the fibre/gut visual, an uplifting marimba swell for the "slow fibre + fluids" solution beat, a soft page-flip for the GLP-1 advisory card, and a calm chime under the disclaimer) to add story-specific color the stock kit can't give, all kept low enough to stay felt rather than heard.
